text: I see some conflicting information in my records, but I will focus on your actual symptoms of wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand what is happening, can you describe how these lesions look and if they are itchy or painful? Also, when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent self-resolving knee pain followed by wrist symptoms, combined with your camping trip in Minnesota and sexual activity, raises concern for disseminated infection. Given your fever and chills, have you had any rashes elsewhere, eye pain, or changes in your urine color? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP; REQUEST TEST: Joint_aspiration_analysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist): WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen. Additional findings from the examination include painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists/hands and a positive Gonorrhea STI screen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI)

The Gram-negative diplococci in your joint fluid, combined with the characteristic painless vesiculopustular skin lesions and positive STI screen, confirm a disseminated gonococcal infection. I have identified the causative organism and the pattern of joint involvement; no further tests are needed to finalize this diagnosis.
